rows.why: Items 1, 2, 3 and 5 each cover part of S1: the header, the BOM, the CRLF endings and the row order. Item 1, about the header row, is the closest. Its run output starts with U+FEFF, has the exact header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created' and ends every line with \r\n. Item 5's run also sorts by createdAt and then id, so every part of S1 holds.

No item asks how status is displayed. The closest match is item 6, on how the creation time is formatted. It writes the full toISOString() value (e.g. 2009-02-13T23:31:30.123Z), but S2 expects just the UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD. The run outputs also show status written as raw 'open' rather than 'Open'. The missing-title part does match (item 7).
Item 4 asks what an empty list produces. Its run returns the BOM plus the header line and nothing else, which is what S3 expects.

Item 8 asks how fields with separators are escaped. Its run quotes a title containing a comma, quotes and \n, and doubles the inner quotes, which matches S4's main rule. S4 also requires quoting for titles that contain \r or start or end with a space. The pick lists only commas, quotes and line breaks, and the run doesn't test spaces, so whether that part holds can't be told.
Item 9 asks about neutralising formula injection. The pick does nothing, and the run writes '@SUM(A1)' and '+3' unchanged. S5 expects a leading single quote before those characters.

Items 10, 11 and 12 together cover S6's invalid cases. Item 12 is the closest because it asks whether a bad row (filled > openings or an invalid date) fails the whole export. It throws an error naming the id ('Requisition bad: ...'). Items 10 and 11 likewise throw with the id for an unknown status and for non-whole-number counts, so all of S6 holds.
